## ECL331 Analog Integrated Circuits & Simulation Lab
This course aims to:
- Familiarize students with the Analog Integrated Circuits and Design and implementation of application circuits using basic Analog Integrated Circuits
- Familiarize students with simulation of basic Analog Integrated Circuits.

### List of experiments
1. I. Fundamentals of operational amplifiers and basic circuits
#### (Minimum seven experiments are to be done)
1. Familiarization of Operational amplifiers – Inverting and Non inverting amplifiers, frequency response, Adder, Integrator, Comparators.
1. Measurement of Op-Amp parameters.
1. Difference Amplifier and Instrumentation amplifier.
1. Schmitt trigger circuit using Op–Amps.
1. Astable and Monostable multivibrator using Op-Amps.
1. Waveform generators using Op-Amps – Triangular and saw tooth
1. Wien bridge oscillator using Op-Amp – without & with amplitude stabilization.
1. RC Phase shift Oscillator.
1. Active second order filters using Op-Amp (LPF, HPF, BPF and BSF).
1. Notch filters to eliminate the 50Hz power line frequency.
1. Precision rectifiers using Op-Amp.
1. II. Application circuits of 555 Timer/565 PLL/ Regulator(IC 723) ICs
#### (Minimum three experiments are to be done)
1. Astable and Monostable multivibrator using Timer IC NE555
1. DC power supply using IC 723: Low voltage and high voltage configurations, Short circuit and Fold-back protection.
1. A/D converters- counter ramp and flash type
1. D/A Converters – R-2R ladder circuit
1. Study of PLL IC: free running frequency lock range capture range
1. III. Simulation experiments (The experiments shall be conducted using SPICE)
1. Simulation of any three circuits from Experiments 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of section I
1. Simulation of Experiments 3 or 4 from section II

[ECL331 lab manual (PDF)](http://ece.cet.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/ECL331-ANALOG-INTEGRATED-CIRCUITS-AND-SIMULATION-LAB-1_compressed.pdf)

## ECL332 Communication Lab
### List of experiments
#### PART A
#### Any two experiments are mandatory. The students shall design and setup simple prototype circuits with the help of available ICs. They can observe Waveforms produced by these circuits for standard ideal inputs.
1. FM generation and demodulation using PLL
1. Generation and Detection of PCM signals
1. Generation and Detection of Delta modulated signals
1. Generation and Detection of BPSK
1. Generation and Detection of 16-QPSK
#### PART B
#### All experiments are mandatory. The students shall write scripts to simulate components of communication systems. They shall plot various graphs that help to appreciate and compare performance.
1. Performance of Waveform Coding Using PCM
1. Pulse Shaping and Matched Filtering Eye Diagram Error Performance of BPSK Error Performance of QPSK
#### PART C
#### Any two experiments are mandatory. The students shall emulate communication systems with the help of software-defined-radio hardware and necessary control software. Use available blocks in GNU Radio to implement all the signal processing. These experiments will help students to appreciate better how theoretical concepts are translated into practice.
1. Familiarization with Software Defined Radio (Hardware and Control Software)
1. FM Reception
1. FM Transmission

## ESL130 Electrical & Electronics Workshop
This course aims to:
- Impart skills to plan and carry out simple electrical wiring.
- To identify the basic practices and safety measures in electrical wiring.

### List of experiments
1. Familiarization/Identification of electronic components with specification (Functionality, type, size, colour coding, package, symbol, cost etc. [Active, Passive, Electrical, Electronic, Electro-mechanical, Wires, Cables, Connectors, Fuses, Switches, Relays, Crystals, Displays, Fasteners, Heat sink etc.)
1. Drawing of electronic circuit diagrams using BIS/IEEE symbols and introduction to EDA tools (such as Dia or XCircuit), Interpret data sheets of discrete components and IC’s, Estimation and costing.
1. Familiarization/Application of testing instruments and commonly used tools. (Multimeter, Function generator, Power supply, DSO etc.) (Soldering iron, Desoldering pump, Pliers, Cutters, Wire strippers, Screw drivers, Tweezers, Crimping tool, Hot air soldering and de- soldering station etc.)
1. Testing of electronic components (Resistor, Capacitor, Diode, Transistor and JFET using multimeter).
1. Inter-connection methods and soldering practice. [Bread board, Wrapping, Crimping, Soldering – types – selection of materials and safety precautions, soldering practice in connectors and general purpose PCB, Crimping.
1. Printed circuit boards (PCB) (Types, Single sided, Double sided, PTH, Processing methods, Design and fabrication of a single sided PCB for a simple circuit with manual etching (Ferric chloride) and drilling.)
1. Assembling of electronic circuits using SMT (Surface Mount Technology) stations.
1. Assembling of electronic circuit/system on general purpose PCB, test and show the functioning (Any Two circuits).
1. Fixed voltage power supply with transformer, rectifier diode, capacitor filter, zener/IC regulator.
1. Square wave generation using IC 555 timer in IC base.
1. Sine wave generation using IC 741 OP-AMP in IC base.
1. RC coupled amplifier with transistor BC107.

This course aims to:
- Familiarize the students with Assembly Language Programming of modern microcontrollers.
- Impart the skills for interfacing the microcontroller with the help of Embedded C/Assembly Language Programming.

1. Sum of a series of 8 bit data.
1. Multiplication by shift and add method.
1. Square / cube / square root of 8 bit data.
1. Matrix addition.
1. LCM and HCF of two 8 bit numbers.

As a technological discipline, computer vision seeks to apply its theories and models to the construction of computer vision systems.
